newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Nov 21.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The volume of mortgage loans approved by Ceskomoravska Hypotecni Banka has exceeded four billion crowns, according to the bank's spokesman, Frantisek Pavelka. The average mortgage loan is for 1.5 million crowns.
- The fourth quarter of 1996 has brought more than 40 billion crowns of new orders to construction companies, raising outstanding orders to 101 billion crowns.
- If the government approves the Minister for Local Development's proposal for the creation of non-profit housing cooperatives, it could mean a decrease in new flat prices by up to one-third.

- With the aim of removing obstacles which exist in domestic economics, the Czech National Bank has called for further deregulation and continuation of the privatisation process, according to CNB Vice-governor Pavel Kysilka.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's adviser has proposed connecting Ceska Sporitelna to a structure of appropriate domestic and foreign investors. This is an alternative to the Czech National Bank's recommendation of merging Ceska Sporitelna with Ceskoslovenska Obchodni Banka (CSOB).
- Bank IPB expects to post a gross profit of 1.6 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of 16 percent. The bank posted a pre-tax profit of 1.29 billion crowns in the first nine months of this year.
- Czech Airlines (CSA) will likely increase fares by three percent effective December 15, according to CSA spokesman, Ivan Bartos.

- Most experts agree that higher voter turnout in the second round of Senate elections will likely mean that the Social Democrats, Civic Democratic Alliance and Christian Democratic Union will obtain more seats. There is also a possibility that different alliances than those that exist in Parliament may arise, according to Borivoj Hnizdo from Charles' University's Faculty of Social Sciences.

- There are currently 700,000 telephone lines in Prague, according to SPT Telecom's Radomir Sabela. Approximately 85 percent of Prague households currently have telephones, he added. On the other hand, there are a record 85,000 outstanding applications for telephones as well.
- Crystalex Novy Bor a.s., the largest domestic producer of crystalware and decorative glass, has formed a new company, Bohemia Crystalex Trading, for the sales of their products.
- Zbrojovka Vsetin has laid off 100 employees effective December 1, in the framework of the company's extensive restructuring plans.
- Receipts for Vychodoceska Plynarenska a.s. increased by 26 percent to 1.898 billion crowns in the first nine months of 1996. Gross profit increased by 2.6 percent to 193 million crowns.
- Turnover posted by ZPS Zlin and its 12 daughter companies reached 3.95 billion crowns in the first three quarters of 1996, an increase of 72 percent over the same period a year earlier.

- According to an analysis of the Internet in the Czech Republic, 92 percent of the users of the Internet are male students or male college graduates. The Internet is accessed at work 54 percent of the time and at school 26 percent of the time. The Internet is used for searching for information relative to work in 49 percent of the cases, entertainment in 20 percent of the cases and education in 19 percent of the cases.

MLADA FRONTO DNES - While Czech Railways posts higher sales, its losses continue to grow. The company expects to lose 4.2 billion crowns by the end of this year, 1.1 billion more than last year and the highest losses since the breakup of the Czechoslovak federation.
- Prices of cigarettes will apparently not increase next year as originally planned since the Ministry of Finance did not approve the necessary increase in the consumer tax on tobacco products.
